name: because, so and that
subtitle: Use because for the reason: I stayed home because I was ill. Use so for the result: I was ill, so I stayed home. After think, hope, know and say, that starts what we think or say, and you can often leave it out: I think (that) it's late.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-a2 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: I stayed home because I was ill. · I was ill, so I stayed home. · I think that it is late.

qa.html: because gives the reason. It answers the question Why? — Why are you late? — Because the bus was late. In a sentence: I stayed home because I was ill. No comma before because.
so gives the result. Put a comma before it: The bus was late, so I missed the train. Same idea, two ways: I went to bed because I was tired. = I was tired, so I went to bed.
that starts what someone thinks, knows, hopes or says: I think that it will rain. She says that she is busy. I'm sure that you will pass. You can leave that out: I think it will rain.
After because, so and that comes a full clause with a subject and a verb: …because I was ill (not because was ill). The word order is the same as in a normal sentence.

Typical mistakes: ✗ Because I was tired, so I went to bed. → ✓ Because I was tired, I went to bed. or I was tired, so I went to bed. (never both) · ✗ I stayed home because was ill. → ✓ …because I was ill. · ✗ I'm late because the traffic. → ✓ I'm late because of the traffic. or …because there was traffic.

concept.noteHtml: A short sentence with because of + a noun also gives a reason: We stayed in because of the rain. Compare: …because it was raining (a clause). The question is always Why? You already know so from and, but, or, so. Here the focus is on reason and result. The verb in the that-clause often needs the right tense: see Present simple and Past simple. Compare can't / have to in Modal verbs.

rounds.label: 1 · Why? — because …
rounds.instruction: You hear a question and the reason. Answer the question with because.

example.prompt: Why are you late? — the bus was late

items.prompt: Why are you tired? — I worked late
Why is Amira happy? — she passed her test
Why are you wearing a coat? — it's cold
Why is Tom at home? — he is ill
Why are you learning English? — I want a new job
items.answer: Because I want a new job.

items.prompt: Why don't you eat meat? — I'm vegetarian

rounds.label: 2 · Reason → result
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence with because. Say the same idea with so: start with the reason.

example.prompt: I took an umbrella because it was raining.
example.answer: It was raining, so I took an umbrella.

items.prompt: I went to bed because I was tired.
items.answer: I was tired, so I went to bed.

items.prompt: She took a taxi because the bus was late.
items.answer: The bus was late, so she took a taxi.

items.prompt: We stayed in because it was cold.
items.answer: It was cold, so we stayed in.

items.prompt: I'm hungry because I didn't have breakfast.
items.answer: I didn't have breakfast, so I'm hungry.

items.prompt: Kwame is happy because he got the job.
items.answer: Kwame got the job, so he's happy.

items.prompt: I can't call you because my phone is broken.
items.answer: My phone is broken, so I can't call you.

exercises.title: because, so or that?
exercises.hint: because = the reason · so = the result · that = what someone thinks, knows, hopes or says.
exercises.hintHtml: becauseThe reason: Why?soThe result: what happens because of it.thatWhat someone thinks, knows, hopes or says.

items.prompt: I stayed home ___ I was ill.
items.why: Being ill is the reason why I stayed home. So: because.

items.prompt: I was ill, ___ I stayed home.
items.why: Staying home is the result of being ill. So: so. ('because' would turn it around.)

items.prompt: I think ___ it's a good idea.
items.why: 'I think ...': what I think comes next. So: that.

items.prompt: The shop is closed ___ it's Sunday.
items.why: Sunday is the reason why the shop is closed. So: because.

items.prompt: It's Sunday, ___ the shop is closed.
items.why: The shop is closed is the result of Sunday. So: so.

items.prompt: She says ___ she's too busy.
items.why: 'She says ...': what she says comes next. So: that.

items.prompt: I'm laughing ___ you look funny!
items.why: You look funny is the reason for my laughing. So: because.

items.prompt: I hope ___ you like the present.
items.why: 'I hope ...': what I hope comes next. So: that.

exercises.title: Say it the other way: reason → result.
exercises.hint: Start with the reason, put a comma, then so + the result. Don't use because and so together.

exercises.title: Leave out that.
exercises.hint: After think, know, hope, say and sure, you can leave out that. The rest stays a full clause with a subject and a verb.

exercises.title: Gap text: A message to a friend.
exercises.hint: Choose because, because of, so or that. Because of comes before a noun. Use that after says, sure and hope.

sentences.hint: The reason first, then a comma and so + the result.
think + that + a new clause (subject + verb).
The answer to Why? Use because + subject + verb.
